summary: Reproduced and repaired the retained-worktree disk leak: ProcessManager._finalize_isolated_request intentionally sets cleanup=False for every non-success terminal state (validation_failed/cancelled/scope_rejected/worker_failed/timed_out/promotion_conflict/finalize_failed) so a human/Codex reviewer can inspect the isolated git worktree + HOME before it is deleted, but nothing ever revisited those retained directories once the coordinator finished reviewing and ran taskctl done/archive -- the workspace stayed on disk forever. Added a fail-closed GC pass (ProcessManager._gc_finalized_workspace(s)) wired into the existing ProcessManager.reconcile() entry point (the same call task_reconciler.py's scan loop already runs on every interval), plus a shared, reusable path-shape validator (worker_workspace.assert_gc_safe_workspace_shape) that re-derives the one legal <configured_root>/<request_id>/{worktree,home} location from request_id alone and never trusts persisted metadata blindly. 26/26 new tests pass; the pre-existing durable-reconciler suite (test_task_liveness_reconciler.py) stays green except two pre-existing, unrelated environment failures (a supervisor heartbeat timing test and a missing scripts/ file, both untouched by this diff -- see known_environment_gaps).

root_cause.description: cleanup=False on every failure terminal path in _finalize_isolated_request is a deliberate, documented design decision (retain evidence for coordinator review), not a bug. The gap is that no code path EVER revisits a retained workspace after the coordinator's own accept/reject decision (taskctl done -> status=finished, or taskctl archive -> archived_at set). ProcessManager only re-scans persisted requests when a NEW instance is constructed or an explicit status/list_processes/reconcile call happens (same structural class of gap as the B411/B412 launcher-loss regression this repo already fixed for exited-but-unfinalized workers), and even then the re-scan only finalizes; it never garbage-collects an already-finalized, already-retained workspace.
root_cause.additional_finding: core._lifecycle_state (tools/aiworkhub/src/aiworkhub/core.py:480-503) never checks card['archived_at'] -- it can only return finished/blocked/review/processing/pending, never 'archived' (AITools/taskdb.py's canonical_status treats a non-empty archived_at as taking priority over every other field). A GC keyed off core._lifecycle_state alone would never become eligible for an archived task; process_launcher._canonical_task_status fixes this locally for the GC path without touching core.py's existing, load-bearing behavior.

worker_workspace_py: Added configured_worktree_root(): factored the WORKTREE_ROOT_ENV/tempdir default computation out of create_workspace() into one shared function so a GC path can re-derive the exact same root create_workspace() itself used, instead of duplicating/drifting the logic.

Added assert_gc_safe_workspace_shape(request_id, path, home): fail-closed shape validator. Re-derives the ONLY legal <configured_worktree_root()>/<request_id>/{worktree,home} pair from request_id alone (after re-validating request_id against _REQUEST_ID_RE) and raises WorkspaceError on any mismatch -- catches a request_id outside the strict grammar, a path/home pair outside the configured root, or a home/worktree swap. Never trusts a request's own persisted metadata path/home strings as proof of safety; GC calls this BEFORE calling the existing cleanup_workspace().
process_launcher_py: Added _canonical_task_status(card): checks card['archived_at'] first (returns 'archived'), else delegates to core._lifecycle_state -- the local fix for core.py's incomplete classifier, scoped to the GC path only.

Added _process_proven_dead(pid, ticks): the fail-closed, opposite-biased counterpart to the existing _pid_matches (which is written to favor 'still the same process' for cancel/liveness). GC needs 'not proven dead' to mean 'do nothing' -- an alive PID with unknown/unrecorded start ticks is NOT proof of death.

Added ProcessManager._gc_finalized_workspace(request_id, event): the single-request, fail-closed GC evaluator. Requires, in order: event.state in GC_CANDIDATE_PROCESS_STATES, event.workspace_retained is true, request_id not in _active_request_ids() (belt-and-suspenders against the in-memory live registry), a readable+parseable *.request.json whose workspace.request_id/repo match exactly, a successful task_id lookup whose canonical status (via _canonical_task_status) is finished or archived, _process_proven_dead(pid, ticks) true, and assert_gc_safe_workspace_shape() passing. Only then calls the EXISTING cleanup_workspace() (already idempotent by construction: existence-guarded git-worktree-remove, ignore_errors=True rmtree) and appends one auditable event that copies the request's own current terminal state unchanged (never altering the task's terminal outcome or any earlier review/release callback transition) plus bounded, non-secret GC evidence fields (workspace_gc, workspace_gc_at, workspace_gc_reason, workspace_retained=false). Every failure mode returns a bounded {'gc': false, 'reason': ...} instead of deleting anything.

Added ProcessManager._gc_finalized_workspaces(): the per-scan sweep over _latest_by_request(), calling _gc_finalized_workspace per candidate (each under its own _registry_lock() critical section, mirroring _reconcile_persisted_requests's existing per-request locking style rather than one lock held across the whole scan).

ProcessManager.reconcile() now also calls _gc_finalized_workspaces() and merges gc_scanned/gc_cleaned/gc_skipped into its return dict -- the ONE required integration point: task_reconciler.py's existing scan loop (daemon or run-once) already calls reconcile() on AIWORKHUB_RECONCILER_SCAN_INTERVAL_SECONDS, so a finalized workspace is swept within one normal reconciliation interval with no new daemon, no cron, and no broad rm -rf.
invariants_preserved: never_weakens_retention: cleanup=False in _finalize_isolated_request is completely untouched; a workspace is retained for review exactly as before. GC only ever acts strictly AFTER the coordinator has independently finished/archived the task.

no_new_task_queue: GC reads the canonical task status through the existing self._show_task (== taskctl show) exactly like every other lifecycle check in this module; it never touches AITools/taskdb.py directly and never adds a second source of truth.

callback_semantics_unchanged: GC never calls core.mark_review or core.release_launch (verified by a dedicated test with monkeypatched spies) and never mutates the task card; only the process-event log and the two on-disk directories are touched.

idempotent_and_fail_closed: a directory that is already gone is a successful no-op (not an error); every ambiguity (missing metadata, unparseable JSON, a failed task lookup, an unproven-dead PID, an unsafe path shape) returns a skip with a reason and deletes nothing.
no_manual_cron: the only entry point is ProcessManager.reconcile(), already driven by task_reconciler.py's existing scan loop; no new script, systemd unit, or cron job was added.

tests.regression_check_result: 21 passed, 2 failed (both pre-existing, unrelated -- see known_environment_gaps)
tests.note_on_test_environment: This isolated worktree lacks aiworkhub/project_context.py -- an uncommitted sibling file in the parent repo not declared in this task's read_first/allowed_writes, so worktree seeding never copied it in. process_launcher.py imports it unconditionally at module scope, so test_task_liveness_reconciler.py (pre-existing, unmodified by this task) fails to collect here too. This test file installs a minimal local stub (mirroring the existing deepseek_credentials stub pattern already used by test_task_liveness_reconciler.py and test_process_launcher_security.py) so the GC logic can be exercised end-to-end in this sandbox; the coordinator's real environment has the real module and needs no stub.

known_environment_gaps.description: Two pre-existing failures observed while regression-checking test_task_liveness_reconciler.py (a file this task did not modify) are environment/sandbox limitations, not caused by this diff:

items.reason: A worker_supervisor.py subprocess/threading timing test (0.1s heartbeat interval, 6s deadline) that observed zero heartbeats in this sandbox's scheduling; worker_supervisor.py was not touched by this diff.

Reads tools/aiworkhub/scripts/geoai-task-reconciler.service, which is missing from this isolated worktree for the same seeding-scope reason as project_context.py (not in read_first/allowed_writes, not yet git-committed).

known_environment_gaps.additional_sandbox_limitation: test_worker_workspace.py, test_process_launcher.py, and test_process_launcher_security.py (none in this task's allowed_writes, none edited) fail in this exact sandbox on unrelated OS-level restrictions -- os.fchmod raising PermissionError and `git init` failing to chmod .git/config.lock. Both are pre-existing sandbox restrictions this exact execution environment imposes (confirmed by the _bridge_chmod_sandbox_restriction fixture already present in the newer test files specifically to probe-and-neutralize this); they are unrelated to the two files this task changed and are expected to pass in the coordinator's real validation environment.

acceptance_status.reproduce_lifecycle_gap: MET -- root_cause above documents the exact code path (cleanup=False, never revisited) and the archived_at classifier gap found alongside it.
acceptance_status.gc_eligibility_rules: MET -- see fix.process_launcher_py; enforced by GC_CANDIDATE_PROCESS_STATES, GC_ELIGIBLE_CANONICAL_STATUSES, _process_proven_dead, _active_request_ids() check, and assert_gc_safe_workspace_shape, each covered by a dedicated test.
acceptance_status.never_delete_uncertain_or_protected_stat: MET -- pending/processing/review/blocked/review_pending/release_pending/reconcile_pending, missing/ambiguous metadata, a live-looking PID, and an unsafe workspace shape are each covered by a dedicated preservation test.
acceptance_status.reuse_cleanup_workspace_idempotent_audit: MET -- GC calls the existing worker_workspace.cleanup_workspace() unchanged, adds no parallel deletion code path, is verified idempotent on both an already-cleaned request and an already-absent directory pair, and appends one auditable event per action with the terminal state preserved.
acceptance_status.integrate_into_existing_reconciler: MET -- wired into ProcessManager.reconcile(), the exact call task_reconciler.py's daemon/run-once loop already drives on its scan interval; no new daemon/cron/script was added.
acceptance_status.targeted_test_coverage: MET -- finalized cleanup, review/blocked/active preservation, PID reuse/start ticks, unsafe path rejection, missing-directory idempotence, and unchanged callback/review lifecycle are each covered by a named test in the list above.
acceptance_status.no_real_worktree_touched_no_task_card_re: MET -- every test uses tmp_path-scoped repos/process dirs/env-overridden WORKTREE_ROOT_ENV; no roadmap, dashboard, or task-card file was edited.

worker_status_recommendation: review -- fail-closed GC implemented, wired into the existing reconciler, and covered by 26 new targeted tests; Codex should independently verify no other call site expects a retained workspace to survive past task finalization before promoting.
